newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: LME zinc poised for fresh assault on $1,450 -trade.
newsitem.headline: LME zinc poised for fresh assault on $1,450 -trade.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) zinc was quoted just below resistance at $1,450 in Asian trade on Wednesday and looked poised to rechallenge the critical barrier later in the day on the LME, dealers said.
At 0500 GMT three-month LME zinc was indicated at $1,445/$1,452 a tonne.

On Tuesday, LME zinc zinc set a new 6-3/4 year high with the cash to three months contango narrowing to $2/$3 a tonne. At 1800 GMT zinc was indicated at $1,445/1,448 against the last trade on the kerb at $1,437, up $9.00.
LME brokers Brandeis and Rudolf Wolff said Tuesday's close was technically bullish for zinc and the metal was now targeting $1,480 if it vaults $1,450.
But Brandeis cautioned zinc was also overbought and this might dampen its challenge on the overhead resistance.
"I guess the zinc prices will firm up. In the later part of the week we feel further strengthening to the $1,450 to $1,475/1,480 levels," one Singapore dealer said.
He said there had recently been a significant amount of speculative and fund buying of zinc.

But other dealers said Asian zinc trading activity had been dampened by the China and Hong Kong holidays so far this week and the metal could undergo a downward correction when these markets returned to business on Thursday.
"We've come to $1,450. there might be some correction....it might fall towards $1,360," one Japanese dealer said.

"The contango between cash/three months narrowed very quickly over the last few days after it stayed at $19-$24 while the zinc price climbed to $1,400 from $1,000. It looks set to turn into backwardation. there's something bothering about it," another Japanese dealer said.
Asian dealers expect three-month LME copper to be stable around the $2,400 level later on Wednesday. The red metal was indicated around the $2,397/2,399 level on the LME on Tuesday.
Brandeis said the copper market was awaiting Wednesday's July option declaration and it expected stiff resistance above the $2,440 level.
Dealers expected LME aluminium to open in London around Tuesday's close of $1,612/1,615 a tonne.
"The opening will be pretty unchanged but it may go up during the day," said one broker.
Brandeis said the aluminium market would face resistance between $1,608 and $1,613.
With the technical indicators trending up and a positive close, further gains on aluminium were favoured, Rudolf Wolff said.
Dealers did not foresee much change in LME lead prices and expected some selling interest in nickel.
